Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials

on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email

  8
 Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

 SUBJECT:  INTRODUCTION  AND  FIRST  READING  OF  ORDINANCE  AUTHORIZING
 AN AMENDMENT  TO THE  CALIFORNIA  PUBLIC  EMPLOYEES'  RETIREMENT  SYSTEM
 CONTRACT  TO  IMPLEMENT  A COST  SHARING  PROGRAM  BETWEEN  THE  CITY  AND
THE  DIVISION  MANAGERS'  ASSOCIATION,  THE  POLICE  MANAGEMENT
ASSOCIATION,  AND  THE  POLICE  OFFICERS'  ASSOCIATION

 PURPOSE:  To introduce  an Ordinance  authorizing  an amendment  to the contract  with  the California
Public  Employees  Retirement  System  ("CalPERS")  to implement  a cost sharing  program  amendment
between  the City  of South Gate ("City")  and the Board  of Administration  of the CalPERS  to implement
 a cost sharing  program  between  the Division  Managers'  Association  ("DMA")  employees,  the Police
Management  Association  ("PMA")  employees,  and  the  Police  Officers'  Association  ("POA")
employees.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  will  consider  waiving  the  reading  in  full  and
introducing  an Ordinance  authorizing  an amendment  to the contract  between  the City  and the Board  of
Administration  of the California  Public  Employees'  Retirement  System  implementing  Section  20516
(Employees  Sharing  Additional  Cost) to provide  employee  cost sharing  of an additional  1% for the local
miscellaneous  members  in the DMA  (for  a total  of 2%),  an additional  1% for the classic  local  police
officers  in the PMA  (for a total of 2%), and for an initial  1% for new ("PEPRA")  local police  members
in both the POA  and PMA.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The  estimated  savings  from  implementing  the cost sharing  program  for  Fiscal
Year 2024-2025  is $72,150.

NOTICING  REQUIREMENTS:  A public  hearing  notice  was duly published  in the South Gate Press,
a newspaper  of general  circulation  on Thursday,  October  10, 2024.

ANALYSIS:  California  retirement  law allows  for two types  of cost sharing  (where  employees  pay a
portion  of the employer  contribution  to CalPERS).  The first type of cost sharing  is by CalPERS  contract
amendment  under  Governrnent  Code (GC)  § 20516(a-e).  In order for cost sharing  to be effective  under
that method,  CalPERS  must first approve  a contract  amendment  with  the City.  This form  of cost sharing
is generally  more  favorable  for employees,  as the additional  employee  contributions  are considered  by
CalPERS  to be "normal  member  contributions"  and are treated  as pre-tax  contributions.  As such, this is
the cost-sharing  method  the City  is proposing.

BACKGROUND:  The City's  current  contract  with  CalPERS  provides  that all employees  pay the full
employee  share toward  their  retirement  benefit.  That  contribution  percentage  differs  based on whether
they  are "Classic"  unit  members  or "PEPRA"  unit  members.  During  the  most  recent  contract
negotiations  between  the City  and the employee  associations,  DMA,  PMA,  and POA,  they agreed that
  1  10
 tliey  would  participate  in a cost  sharing  program.  The  South  Gate  Police  Management  Association
("PMA")  was the first labor group  to participate  in the cost sharing  program  by having  all their "Classic"
unit members  contribute  2% of their  salary toward  the City's  share of their retirement  benefits  beginning
in FY 2022-23.  The PEPRA  members  of PMA  did not initiate  their  cost sharing  at that time  and, as part
of this action,  they will  now participate  in the same manner  as their "Classic"  counterparts.  The final
ordinance  amending  the CalPERS  contract  for the cost sharing  program  with  PMA  for  its "Classic"
members  was approved  by the City  Council  at its February  14, 2023, meeting.

The other employee  associations,  the Miscellaneous  Employees'  Association  ("MEA"),  the Professional
Mid-Management  Association  ("PMMA"),  the Division  Managers'  Association  ("DMA"),  and the
Police  Officers'  Association  ("POA"),  followed  with members  agreeing  to participate  in the cost sharing
program  by contributing  1% of their salary toward  the City's  share of their retirement  benefits  beginning
in FY 2023-24.  This ordinance  amending  the CalPERS  contract  for the cost sharing  program  with  MEA,
PMMA,  DMA,  and POA  was approved  by the City  Council  at its June 13, 2023,  meeting.  The cost
sharing  program  for each of these labor groups  is pursuant  to California  Governrnent  Code 20516(a)  and
was effective  in July  2023.  The final  ordinance  amending  the CalPERS  contract  for the cost sharing
program  with  the Executive  Management  Group  was approved  by the City  Council  at its November  26,
2023,  meeting.  The  cost sharing  program  for this  group  is pursuant  to California  Government  Code
20516(a)  and was effective  on December  31, 2023.

Staff began working  with  CalPERS  to 'further  amend the City's  contract  to implement  agreed  additional
contributions  by DMA,  PMA,  and POA  members,  which  is to provide  an additional  1%  for  local
miscellaneous  member  in DMA,  an additional  1%  for  classic  members  of the POA,  and an 1%  for
PEPRA  members  of PMA.  Staff initiated  this process with  CalPERS  in May  2024 and received  approval
and the necessary  information  to move  forward  on July 17, 2024.  The additional  amounts  paid by the
employee  toward  the City's  contribution  will  be credited  to each member's  PERS  account  as normal
contributions  and will  allow  the City  to process  the full  contribution  as tax deferred  compensation  in
accordance  with  IRC414(h)(2).

In order to proceed  with  amending  the City's  contract  with  CalPERS  for cost sharing,  CalPERS  requires:

  1.  A Resolution  of Intention,  which  the City  Council  issued  on August  13, 2024;
  2.  An election  of employees  agreeing  to the contract  change;  and
  3.  An adoption  of an ordinance  amending  the City's  contract  with  CalPERS.

At its August  13, 2024, meeting,  City  Council  adopted  Resolution  No. 2024-59-CC  declaring  its intent
to amend  the contract  with  CalPERS  to implement  a cost sharing  program.  Furthermore,  the members
of PMA  and POA  conducted  a secret ballot  election,  as certified  by the City  Clerk  on September  3, 2024,
providing  that a majority  of the groups  voted  in favor  of the proposed  cost sharing  program.  The final
step to amend  the contract  is to adopt  an ordinance  authorizing  an amendment  to the contract  between
the City  and CalPERS.  Today's  meeting  is to waive  the reading  in full  and introduce  an ordinance
authorizing  an amendment  to the contract.  Staff will  then come back for final  adoption  of the ordinance
at the November  12, 2024,  City  Council  meeting.

SECTION  4.  If any section,  subsection,  subdivision,  sentence,  clause,  phrase,  or portion  of this

  SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  DECLARING  A  CONTINUED  EMERGENCY  AND
  AUTHORIZING  REPAIR,  REPLACEMENT  OR  MAINTENANCE  ACTIVITIES  OF
  PUBLIC  FACILITIES  RELATED  TO  THE  URBAN  ORCHARD,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.
  539-PRK  WITHOUT  PUBLIC  BIDDING,  PURSUANT  TO  THE  EMERGENCY
  CONTRACTING  PROCEDURES  OF  THE  SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE  AND
  THE  CALIFORNIA  PUBLIC  CONTRACT  CODE

  PURPOSE:  To declare  an emergency  still  exists  and to authorize  the repair,  replacement  or

  maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard  Project  without  public
  bidding.  The  Los  Angeles  County  Department  of  Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Division
  ("County")  issued  a Corrective  Action  Order  requiring  construction  to stop on the project.  The
  declaration  of  emergency  is necessary  to  streamline  the  process  to procure  a replacement
  contractor  to provide  maintenance  activities  to preserve  the site in a safe condition  until  the
  County  authorizes  construction  work  on the project  to resume.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider  making  a finding  and adopting
  Resolution  declaring  an  emergency  still  exists  and  authorizing  repair,  replacement  or
  maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard,  City  Project  No.  539-
  PRK,  without  public  bidding,  pursuant  to the emergency  contracting  procedures  of the South
  Gate Municipal  Code and the California  Public  Contract  Code.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no  impact  to the  General  Fund.  The  Urban  Orchard  Project
  ("Project")  has received  a total of $30.5 million  in grant and other funds  for design,  construction,
  operations,  and maintenance,  as summarized  below.

  ANALYSIS:  The Project  was under  construction  and approximately  90% of construction  work
  has been  completed.  On  December  29,  2022,  the  City  received  a Corrective  Action  Order
  ("Order")  from  the County.  The Order  required  the City  to stop all construction  activities  until
  such a time as a Post Closure  Land Use Plan ("PCLUP")  for the Project  site was approved  by the
  County.  Given  the PCLUP  approval  process  and input  received  to date,  it will  take  at least
  several  months,  possibly  six or more,  to obtain  approval.

  To  avoid  the  significant  delay  damages  that  would  be payable  by  the  City  to the  general
  contractor  during  a prolonged  suspension  of the project  pending  approval  of the PCLUP,  the City

  1
  25
 Council  ten'ninated  the general  contractor's  agreement  at a Special  City  Council  meeting  on
February  6, 2023.  Such ten'nination  provided  both  iininediate  and long-ten'n  cost savings  to the
City  but also created  an immediate  need for the City  to retain  an interim  contractor  to perfon'n
certain  ongoing  maintenance  and safety  activities;  a need whicli  must  be met  sooner  than  the
time necessary  to engage in normal  public  bidding  procedures

The proposed  Resolution  declares  a continued  emergency  exists pursuant  to the authority  granted
by South  Gate Municipal  Code  § 1.54.470  and California  Public  Contract  Code  § 22050.  Those
Code  Sections  allow  cities,  by resolution,  to approve  the City's  entry  into  contracts  without
engaging  in public  bidding  where  certain  emergency  conditions  are found  to have occurred.  Staff
continues  to believe  that the County's  Order  directing  all construction  work  to be ceased on the
Project,  constitutes  such an emergency  due to the public's  safety  with  an unfinished  construction
site and the need to respond  accordingly  to additional  directives  given  by the County  related  to
ensuring  public  safety.  Staff  are recominending  that  the  City  Council  adopt  the  proposed

 ANALYSIS:  The City owns and operates a municipal water and sanitary sewer system which it
maintains through City forces and maintenance contractors. The City has a contract with Rasic
for as-needed emergency sewer and water system repairs, which is utilized to complete repairs
of issues beyond the City's staffing capacity to complete on a timely basis.

On August 6, 2024, a sinkhole was exposed by the construction on Long Beacli Boulevard  at its
intersection with Firestone Boulevard. The sinkhole was caused by an abandoned sewer lateral,
which had collapsed. The leaking sewage caused the pavement to undermine, creating a void
seven feet deep, eight feet long, and 15 feet wide. Staff authorized Rasic to complete repairs of
the sinkhole and sewer lateral on an emergency basis to make the street safe and passable for
vehicular and pedestrian traffic. The total cost was $72,140.

The Hawkins Reservoir ("Reservoir")  is a water production facility serving the water system.
Amongst other, it is operated with water valves that are critical to operate water flow into and
out of the Reservoir and to isolate water flows in an event of an emergency.  Urgent repairs are
needed to replace two large broken water valves in the distribution system irni'nediately  entering
the Reservoir at 9027 Frontage Road and one large water valve at Firestone Boulevard near the
I-7 10 Freeway. A proposal was received from Rasic in the amount of $136,000.

Amendment  No. 5 is needed to fund these repairs, for a total amount of $208,140.

BACKGROUND:  The Project is a part of the CIP. It is under construction and nearing
completion.  During constniction  of the roadway, a sinkhole was discovered that required
iinmediate repairs. Rasic was authorized to complete the repairs under Contract No. 2020-09-
CC. The repairs involved filling the sinkhole, capping the lateral pipe, replacing the street
pavement and related work. Work began on August 6, 2024, and was completed on August 28'h,
The fees for the repairs were $72,140 of which $26,798 was to repair the sink hole and $45,342
to restore the concrete bus pad and street pavement. City Staff reviewed the cost and found it to
be fair and reasonable. These repairs qualify to be funded with projects funds as the repairs are
needed for the completion  of the project.

The repairs to the water system require the resources provided by the Agreement. Condition is
such as the services and equipment of a specialized contractor are warranted to safely complete
the work involved. The 12" water main is approximately  six to eight feet deep, which will
require shoring and specialized equipment to safely perform the repair. The water main is
Cement Mortar Lined Steel Pipe which requires welding that in-house staff does not have the
capability to provide. The work near the I-710 also requires a traffic control plan and Cal Trans
permit as it will impact traffic on the off ramp. The Rasic $136,000 fee proposal is in line with
the agreement.

On January 28, 2020, the City entered into an Agreement  with  Rasic to perform  emergency
repairs on the municipal water and sanitary sewer systems in the amount $300,000, or $100,000
annually. The contract was awarded pursuant to a competitive bid process.

On August 10, 2021, Amendment No. 1 was approved to fund emergency  repairs that were
perfornned to, (a) replace a leaking 20-inch valve located on the municipal water system

 ANALYSIS:  The Public  Works  Department  utilizes  the services  of a maintenance
 contractor  to provide  landscaping  and general  maintenance  on City  facilities  and landscaped

  1
  114
 areas  in the public  riglit-of-way.  The current  agreement  with  Parkwood  Landscape
Maintenance,  Inc.  ("Parkwood")  expires  October  31, 2024. A replacement  contract  is needed.
Mariposa  Landscape,  Inc.  ("Mariposa")  is recommended  for the new contract.

The proposed  Agreement  provides  $1,197,513  for year-round  maintenance  services  and
$163,500  for emergency  response  services,  annually.  It is for a three-year  tenn  for an
amount  of $1,361,016,  or $453,672,  annually,  starting  November  1, 2024.  It is noted  that
Mariposa's  bid  amount  was $1,252,013  inclusive  of $1,197,513  forthree  years  of annual
maintenance  services  plus  $54,500  for one year  of emergency  response  services.  Staff  is
recommending  the proposed  Agreement  include  emergency  response  services  for Year  2
and Year  3 of the contract,  for an annual  amount  of $54,500,  to cover  unforeseen  damages
and circumstances.  As sucli,  the recommended  contract  includes  an additional  $109,003,  for
a grand  total  of $1,361,016.

Mariposa's  bid for three  years  of general  maintenance  services  is lower  than  Salazar
Landscaping's  bid by $86,003.  Their  three-year  proposal  amount  for emergency  response
services  is $163,500  as compared  to Salazar's  bid of $64,750.  Note  that these are budgetary
figures.  The City  of South  Gate ("City")  will  incur  emergency  response  expenses  based  on
the number  of incidents  in the field  that occur  annually,  where  each contractor  would  charge
based  on time  and materials.  The final  actual  amount  to be paid  is not limited  by these
budgetary  figures.  Also,  Mariposa's  fees are approximately  $70,000  greater  than the current
contract  cost; however,  Parkwood's  fees are based  on a 2021  pricing  structure,  whereas  the
Mariposa's  fees are based  on 2024  pricing  structure.  Further,  the scope  of work  has
increased  amid  newly  constructed  hardscape  infrastructure  (street  medians)  located  on Long
Beach  Boulevard  and Garfield  Avenue  and additional  landscape  square  footage  from  vacant
properties  on Paramount  Boulevard  and Willow  Place;  sound  wall  and parkways  at West
Frontage  Road,  and the Urban  Orchard  Park  entrances.  That  said, Mariposa's  fees were
determined  to be reasonable.

The contract  provides  for two  independent,  one-year  contract  term  extensions.  The City
Council  is recommended  to authorize  the City  Manager  to administratively  approve  these
two  term  extensions.  The extensions  will  be at the City  Manager's  discretion  based  on the
recommendations  for the Department  of Public  Works  and the successful  performance  of
Mariposa.

BACKGROUND:  The City  owns facilities  citywide  that require  landscaping  and general
maintenance  services.  This  includes  facilities  such as landscaped  road medians,  city-owned
vacant  properties,  retaining  walls,  bus shelters,  sidewalks,  parking  lots, the Tweedy  Mile  District,
and the Hollydale  Shopping  Center.  The Department  of Public  Works  maintains  these facilities
through  the services  of a maintenance  contractor  that provide  annual  maintenance  services  as
well  as emergency  responses  services.  Currently,  these facilities  are maintained  by Parkwood,
under  Contract  No. 2021-127-CC.  The agreement  expires  on October  31, 2024.

On August  19, 2024, a Request  for Proposal  ("RFP")  was issued to procure  a new contract.  On
September  12, 2024, two proposals  were received  in the City  Clerk's  Office,  as summarized  on
the next page. A panel comprised  of the Streets  Supervisor  and the Streets and Sewer

  2
  115
 Superintendent, interviewed the contractors on October 1, 2024. The panel rated tliem based on
the criteria detailed in the RFP and bestowed the highest qualitative appraisal to Mariposa. Tlie
appraisal assessed Mariposa's qualifications, organizational capacity, current and past public
sector contracts, directly related public sector experience, and expertise levels.

Contract services include landscape and general maintenance services for the Tweedy  Mile
Shopping District, the Hollydale Shopping District, roadway medians citywide, and water
well sites. It also provides services for bus stops and shelters, the Alameda Sound Wall,
parking lots and other municipal facilities. The contract scope of work includes mowing,
edging, weeding, pruning, fertilization,  seasonal planting, trash pick-up, pest control, upkeep
of the irrigation systems, steam cleaning of bus shelters and sidewalks, and other landscape
and general maintenance tasks. It also includes maintenance for annual special events such
as the Children's Christmas Lane Parade, Street Fair, and Posadas on Tweedy Boulevard.

The proposed Agreement also includes annual emergency  response  services.  This service  is
needed to address unforeseen field conditions  that require  maintenance  on a priority  and
timely basis. Emergency  Response  Services  include  repairs  to existing  landscapes  and
irrigation systems that become damaged,  such as by a vehicle  accident.  Work  typically
includes replacing and replanting  landscape  material,  repairing  damage  to irrigation
systems,  and vandalism.

Mariposa has rendered their services to the City through previous  landscape contracts from
2012 and ending 2018. Mariposa returns to the City with 45 years of experience  and over
800 employees. They value long-lasting  relationships with their clients which currently
include the cities of Bell, Vernon, Baldwin Park and Santa Monica. They possess the ability
to better adhere to the scope of work outlined in the RFP in terms of experience  with multiple
municipal contracts, and resource availability. They possess the resources,  equipment and
manpower to perfonn the work. Mariposa also has experience  working in the City. They were
the City's landscape maintenance contractor for six years.

  ANALYSIS:  The City  of South  Gate ("City")  owns  and operates  a municipal  water  system  that

  in water  rights  and a water  demand  of 7,800  AF,  leaving  an estimated  balance  of 3,383  AF.
  These  unused  water  rights  cargovers  annually  but  are subject  to lapse  if the storage  balance

BACKGROUND:  Tlie  City  owns  and operates  a municipal  water  system  that serves  drinking
water  to  over  14,300  customers.  The  water  system  is 100%  dependent  on  groundwater.
Groundwater  is extracted  by  water  wells  within  the  Central  Basin.  It  is tlien  pumped  into
reservoirs  or tl'ie water  distribution  system.

The Central  Basin  is adjudicated,  which  requires  autliorization  to extract  groundwater.  The City
owns water  rights,  which  give the City  the authority  to extract  and serve groundwater  as drinking
water.  These  unused  water  riglits  carryover  annually  but  are subject  to lapse  if  the  storage
balance  exceeds  200%  of tl'ie City's  adjudicated  APA.  To prevent  water rights  from  lapsing,  staff
is recommending  tlie lease of 1,000  AF in water  rights  aniiually  to the City  of Cerritos.  This  will
'further  provide  revenue  for the next three years.

A Request  for Proposal  ("RFP")  was issued  to competitively  select lease agreements  on August
13,  2024.  One  bid was received  from  the  City  of  Cerritos.  The  bid amount  was  $180,000
annually  or $180  dollar  per acre foot.  The  City  of South  Gate has been leasing  unused  water
rights  to the City  of Cerritos  for the last ten years, primarily  to prevent  them from  lapsing,  and to
generate  revenue  for tlie Water  Fund.  As such, staff recorni'nends  awarding  the lease to Cerritos.

ANALYSIS:  The Engineering  Consultants will each provide the following  services:

  *  As-needed Engineering Services - Comt'non as-needed engineering service needs include
  execution of miscellaneous technical assigni'nents, plan check, development review, survey
  services, legal descriptions and tract map reviews.

  *  Grant  Writing  Services  Preparation  of applications  for grant funds,  and funding
  administration.

  *  As-neededCIPSupportServices-Comi'nonservicesincludeperformingplanchecksofCIP
  projects, reviewing technical studies, reviewing or preparing prevailing wage compliance

In addition, Willdan Engineering will provide as-needed ProjectManagement Services to implement
capital improvement projects. Whereas As-needed CIP Support Services consist of the comi'non
services noted above, Project Management Services consists of managing assigned projects from
design through construction. Under these services, Willdan Engineering assigns projects managers
based on the capital projects the City assigns to them. These services are needed to continue the
implantationofongoingprojects.  TheCIPhasover$100Millioninfundedprojectsandadditional
project management resources as needed to complete projects on schedule and meet funding
requirements.

BACKGROUND:  Since 2004, the Public Works Department has used as-needed engineering
services to provide the Engineering Division  with specialized technical services,  enhanced
engineering expertise, and staffing support. As-needed engineering  services are essential to expedite
the completion of miscellaneous engineering services not commonly offered by full-time staff. By
using this approach, the Public Works Department has been successful in delivering numerous CIP
projects and in securing grants. The proposed Engineering Consultants will provide the as-needed
engineering  services.

The Engineering Division's  capacity to implement projects timely is currently impacted by
engineering vacancies. The two Principal Civil Engineering positions are still vacant. Under the
current contract, Willdan Engineering is providing project management services. The proposed as-
needed project management services are needed to continue implementation ofprojects thatWilldan
Engineering is currently implementing.

Dear Mr. Osuna,
The City of South Gate is seeking consultants to provide as needed engineering services that may include
engineering and architectural design, construction management, inspection, geotechnical, project
management, staff augmentation, surveying, special funding administration, grant writing, plan review,
right-of-way acquisition, assessment district engineering, estimating, arborist services, preparation of
grant and federal funding reimbursement requests, traffic, and transportation engineering. As a
multidisciplinary firm, Willdan Engineering (Willdan) has a full complement of resources under one roof,
enabling us to provide a complete range of services to the City of South Gate. Willdan has assembled a
team of highly qualified and deeply experienced individuals who are fully committed to the successful
completion of assignments under this contract.
Our firm has over 60-years of experience providing a wide range of support services to local government
agencies throughout Southern California and the Western United States, including all services being
requested by the City. Because we focus solely on the needs of the public sector, we have a perspective
on public agency issues that is unique among private consulting firms.
We believe there are several reasons why Willdan is uniquely qualified to undertake this important
assignment for the City of South Gate:
Knowledge of the City – Willdan’s knowledge of the City of South Gate and our experience in providing a
wide range of services to the City for the past 25 years, will enable us to initiate work quickly and to
respond appropriately to issues that arise during the course of this contract. We currently provide
construction management and inspection services, planning and staff augmentation, building and safety
services, on-call traffic engineering services, general engineering services, design engineering and special
district services to the City of South Gate. For this reason, we have an established working relationship
with City staff and a familiarity with City procedures and requirements.
60-Year Track Record – Willdan has extensive experience providing a complete range of engineering
services to local agencies on an “as-needed” basis and for specific projects. The firm’s capabilities
encompass streets and highways, drainage, water/wastewater, signals, traffic programs, bridges and
structures, landscaping, and mapping. We provide professional services in all phases of project
development, including site analysis and conceptual development; preliminary and final design; and

 Understanding of City’s Needs
  Willdan currently provides all of the identified services outlined in the City’s RFQ and is prepared to meet
  all of the conditions specified. Willdan is well qualified to provide the requested services to the City of
  South Gate.
  Since 1964, Willdan has provided consulting services to hundreds of public agencies in the western United
  States. Our depth of experience and broad range of capabilities allow Willdan to offer comprehensive
  resources for efficient and convenient service. In addition, our expertise in the engineering and planning
  fields ensures innovative and effective solutions will be applied to all projects undertaken by Willdan.
  Many of our specialists have a strong background and an intimate understanding of diverse programs for
  public agencies. This expertise provides the foundation for planning, design, inspection, and
  administration under agency programs, and offers added value with our unique familiarity with state- and
  federally-funded programs. We also place strong emphasis on communication and maintaining personal
  interaction with the community at large.
  Our project approach begins with designating a complete project management team. Each project
  management team will be led by a principal representative with full authority to direct operations and
  commit resources. In addition to the principal representative, the management team will include expert
  staff specializing in the type of service requested. Our array of in-house experts allows Willdan to develop
  a specialized management team for each requested project.
  In addition, Willdan’s size gives us the flexibility to undertake large projects and projects on a compressed
  time schedule. If a project arises that requires immediate or extra attention, Willdan’s flexibility allows
  tasks to be rapidly delegated to an expanded team of staff members. This ensures that the project will
  receive appropriate attention to detail and be completed in a timely fashion.
  The first task of Willdan’s delegated project management team will be to establish a course of action. This
  task will begin by coordinating with the City to identify specific project objectives. With these objectives
  in mind, Willdan’s experienced professionals will actively identify areas of need and design solutions to
  address these needs. Our policy of open and often client coordination will ensure the established course
  of action and will be consistent with the City’s goals.
  Once the course of action is established, Willdan will develop a project schedule. Each project schedule
  will be developed with the City’s project completion date in mind and will include a critical path and
  measurable milestones to ensure the project completion date is met. All project schedules will be
  submitted to the City to guarantee consistency with the City’s timeline.
  In enacting and completing the course of action, Willdan strives to exceed client expectations for quality
  of work. Willdan has a history of completing projects on time, within budget, and beyond industry
  standards. Willdan is committed to providing this level of service to the City. As such, after each project is
  completed, Willdan will follow-up with the City to gather feedback on the City’s satisfaction with the
  project, and to identify methods to improve future service.

 Communication Approach
Willdan recognizes that effective, ongoing cooperative
communication between all parties over the course of
any assignment is essential to successful project
completion. This communication starts with a project
kick-off meeting where the objectives and expectations of
the City for each task order/assignment are clearly
articulated and understood by Willdan. In addition,
agreed-upon methods and scheduling of formal reporting
are established with identification of individuals to be
involved in the project's decision-making process. This
sets forth accountability and responsibility for informing and facilitating the project. As the project
progresses, communication continues through regular correspondence, teleconference discussions, and
meetings with City staff seeking direction on issues that may arise and keeping City staff apprised of the
project. Clear and concise progress updates are provided. Emails and teleconferences are utilized
whenever possible and appropriate to minimize City staff time spent in meetings.
Methodology
Willdan's methodology focuses heavily on client service and communications. As a firm with a strong
public agency orientation, many of our client relationships are long-term and ones in which our staff
develops intimate familiarity with the client's staff since we very often serve as an extension of public
agency staff. As such, it is extremely important that our presence on each assignment is seamless.
Willdan's staff assigned as Project Manager, City Engineer, Land Surveyor, Traffic Engineer, Building
Official, and other higher-level positions most often work independently of the other project team
members, since they are generally working directly for and with public agency staff as a part of the
agency's staff. In this instance, the project team’s role is subservient to the primary assignment and only
comes into play on a support basis or on a project-specific basis, such as for additional services for capital
improvement project design, reviewing tract and parcel maps, and structural assessments.

Technical Approach
As previously stated, upon receipt of a project assignment or award, our project management will analyze
the project and assign a Discipline Manager with the appropriate qualifications and experience to ensure
tasks are completed in accordance with the City's goals and visions. Together, they will select qualified
team members to provide technical support for the project. We will convey all-important matters to the
assigned Discipline Manager and the selected project team as appropriate. The Discipline Manager will,
then, take full responsibility for understanding the project requirements, detailing the project scope
requirements, and estimating the fee to complete the project effectively and efficiently. The assigned
Discipline Manager will maintain the team members assigned to the project from beginning to end. This
means the same individuals responsible for design elements are the same individuals reviewing shop
drawings, preparing as-built plans, or responding to questions during the bidding or construction process.
This management approach has been proven on past projects to be effective in delivering projects on
time, within budget and to the client’s satisfaction.

 Project Kick-Off Meetings – All project team members will meet to discuss and clarify the project
  scope, schedule, and other pertinent information related to the service or project. This meeting is
  conducted upon receipt of the notice to proceed and prior to any work being performed. This meeting

  are responsible for keeping the City up to date on project status and issues raised throughout the
  project. This is accomplished through regular meetings, written status reports, or other means of
  communication requested.
  Periodic Updates through Project Status Meetings – At the project kick-off meeting, the project team
  determines and selects meeting dates throughout the project to discuss coordination, issues, changes,
  and other information necessary to keep the project on track in terms of quality, schedule, and
  budget.
  Objective Review of Project by Peers – Prior to the submittal of a project to the City, appropriate staff
  members review the project to ensure all information is accurate. Willdan staff conducting these
  reviews are not directly involved with the project – enabling objectivity in the review. Depending
  upon the complexity of the project, the four levels of our quality assurance review for project
  deliverables may entail:
    Level 1 – peer review only
    Level 2 – peer review and editorial review (documents)
    Level 3 – peer review, editorial review, and professional engineer review
    Level 4 – all elements of Level 3 plus additional reviews by specific technical experts

and not directly involved in the assignments to implement project-specific quality assurance activities.
Each senior member of staff will report directly to Adel but work closely with the Task Managers to ensure
project objectives are met at project completion. Random audits will be conducted to ensure proper
quality assurance activities have been accomplished with necessary corrective actions taken. These audits
involve verifying task completion, validating the quality review, confirming comments resolution, and
verifying that agreed-upon changes are reflected in each affected document. Adel will regularly seek
feedback on how Willdan's team is performing and how we can improve upon the level of service.

lnterwest’s management philosophy is to retain senior-level employees who have years of experience in their

with the Department of Public Works and other City personnel, applicants, and designers to resolve issues as

Sub-Consultants
Interwest proposes to use the following sub-consultants for project assigned under this contract for
specialty services not typically provided by our in-house team of professionals. We have a long-standing
relationship with these firms and can attest to the quality of their work product.

Ninyo & Moore (Geotechnical Engineering & Materials Testing)
Ninyo & Moore, a certified Minority Business Enterprise (MBE), was established
as a California corporation in 1987 to provide geotechnical engineering,
engineering geology, materials testing and inspection, and environmental
consulting services to clients in the governmental (federal, state, and local) and commercial sectors.
N&M services encompass every stage of a project, from project feasibility studies through planning,
design build, design and construction. During the past 38 years, N&M has grown to 600 dedicated
professionals with long-term, demonstrated experience on geotechnical, environmental, materials
testing and inspection services on public infrastructure projects.
Providing geotechnical, materials testing and inspection, and environmental consulting services for
various public agencies has been a major part of N&M’s work throughout its 36-year history. The firm
has successfully completed work on hundreds of roadways/street resurfacing improvements, including
hundreds of highway structures throughout California and the western United States for the Caltrans
District 8, 12, 11, & 7, Orange County Transportation Authority, Riverside County Transportation
Department, Riverside County Transportation Commission, San Bernardino County Transportation
Authority, the Federal Highway Administration, Transportation Corridor Agency, and other local
government agencies.

UNICO Engineering, Inc. (Survey and Mapping)
Established in 2013, UNICO Engineering is a certified DBE firm that is fully
committed to providing high quality construction management, engineering,
and land surveying services to public and private clients. UNICO serves clients throughout California with
a current staff of over 90 from our corporate office located in Folsom, with branch offices in Concord,
Oakland, San Diego, and Goleta, and field offices in Sacramento, Woodland, Paradise, and Angels
Camp. Their success is measured by the success of their clients, their responsiveness, and the quality
and value of their work. Top on their priority list is to understand clients’ objectives and expectations.
They provide value to our clients by sharing the goal of effectively managing the costs of the projects
which we are assigned. Their survey team has the technology and experience to address any of the City’s
surveying needs, including topographic mapping, bathymetric (hydrographic) surveys, ALTAs, boundary
surveys, construction staking, easements, aerial surveys, right of ways, terrestrial LiDAR scanning and
drone surveying. Using the latest in GPS and robotic total station technology, Unico works efficiently
and delivers accurate results. They are experienced in delivering projects that meet local, state, and
federal requirements.

Understanding of City’s Needs
NV5 can provide professional, comprehensive engineering services on a per project or task order basis
for all types of capital improvement projects. NV5 can provide the City with a full range of professional
engineering services covering the following areas, including, but not limited to: engineering design,
construction management, inspection, geotechnical, project management, staff augmentation,
surveying, special funding administration (intergovernmental agencies), grant writing, plan review, right-
of-way acquisition (with legal descriptions and appraisals), assessment district engineering, estimating,
preparation of grant and federal funding reimbursement requests, traffic and transportation engineering.
Below is our general project approach that will be modified and tailored to meet each project’s needs.

Approach to Services
NV5 can provide professional, comprehensive engineering services on a per project or task order basis for
all types of capital improvement projects. Below is our general project approach that will be modified and
tailored to meet each project’s needs.
WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE
Upon issuance of a notice to proceed, our project manager will meet with team members to review the
requirements, prepare a Work Breakdown Structure and make team assignments for maximum efficiency
of resources. The detailed WBS will describe all of the work tasks necessary to complete the project. A
master project schedule will be prepared following the WBS to show the relationship between tasks, the
expected start date and duration for each item. This schedule will serve as a guide to conducting and
monitoring the progress of the work and to assure projects are completed on time and within budget. To
assure accurate monitoring and tracking of documents, revisions and progress, a document tracking and
control system will be developed. NV5 will meet with City project representatives regularly and maintain
constant communication to assure successful and timely delivery of the project. Meeting minutes will be
distributed within one week of the meeting identifying actions, items, assignments and due dates.
COST CONTROL
We are able to continually review and evaluate a project’s cost through all project phases to enable
informed and timely decision-making by our clients and the entire project team. Cost control techniques
include: program budget analysis; value engineering; life-cycle cost analysis; and quantity-based
estimating. We rely on an open-book, inclusive process that demonstrates the costs and benefits of varying
design options. This budget confirmation process starts in the earliest stages of the project, when design
and engineering alternatives have the greatest potential impact on costs. Our design teams analyze client
goals, technical requirements, alternative building concepts, construction costs and long-term operational
costs to define the optimum scope within the budget, assuring long-term flexibility and value.
SCHEDULE CONTROL
The key to effective schedule control is to measure actual progress and compare it to planned progress
on a regular basis and to take necessary corrective action immediately. We propose to supplement each
major task as identified in the master project schedule with a supplemental schedule to keep careful track
of where each individual component stands. We identify problems that may result from delays and readily
provide the opportunity to modify the schedule, as required. This process assures the completion of your
projects on schedule.

INNOVATIVE AND SUCCESSFUL APPROACHES
The NV5 team focuses on providing safe, cost-effective, reliable, and sustainable improvements using
innovative design and contracting techniques that meet or exceed the minimum standards based on
design improvements and minimize impacts to adjacent properties and vehicular and pedestrian traffic.
Our experienced engineering staff provides lower-cost or lower-impact alternatives in order to develop the
least disruptive and least expensive designs.
One such example of our use of innovative techniques can be seen in our work on the design of the
Industrial Way Storm Drain and Drainage Improvements project for the City of Costa Mesa.
The project included design of a drainage system to alleviate the flooding in the area. The existing 48-inch
storm drain pipe in the street (Industrial Way) was not capable of handling the storm flood in its current
condition. We studied different design options and performed hydrology and hydraulic analysis for various
alternatives. We designed a system that would limit the flow into the existing storm drain system. In
addition, we designed an underground detention system consisting of three (3) rows of 12-inch, perforated
corrugated metal pipes within the available portion of the adjacent field. The new drainage system solved
the flooding problem in the area and saved the City Public Works Department a substantial amount of
money. The proposed design alternative was much superior to a conventional trenching method within the
street area consisting of replacing a large segment of the existing pipe with a larger diameter pipe and
adding numerous catch basins. The construction of the new drainage system was completed on time and
it is working just as intended.
Our team utilizes the latest in civil engineering design software to facilitate timely, efficient, and innovative
engineering design solutions for our clients. We rely on a host of computer resources, which includes up-

Deliverables
Deliverables for a typical plan check project include:

  • Redlined plans
In compliance with state law, all plan check services will be performed by or under the responsible charge

study being reviewed. All plan review memos will be signed and sealed by a duly licensed professional.
Submittal Sequence
Each submittal will generally follow the following sequence:
First Plan Check
The initial plan check will be comprehensive and identify all significant issues. It is important to present
significant issues to the developer as early in the review process as possible, so that the developer can
respond in a timely manner. In addition to the typical scope of services, the first plan check will include the
following:
  • Plan Review Checklist
  • Review of Conditions of Discretionary Approval
  • Analysis of Easement Requirements and Right-Of-Way Needs
  • Identification of Required Coordination with Inter-Agency Jurisdictional Issues
Subsequent Submittals
Plan check resubmittals are reviewed for completeness and to determine if all previous comments
have been fully addressed. If the developer has made significant changes to the submittal, new review
comments may be necessary. The NV5 plan checker will identify remaining deficiencies in the documents
for subsequent reiterations of the plan check submittals.
Final Review
We anticipate that after no more than three (3) plan checks, NV5 will request that the developer submit
final plans and associated documents, as required by the City for final review. NV5 will confirm that plans
are complete and that all associated documents have been submitted. NV5 will then provide an approval
letter and other required documents and transmittals, depending on the type of review.
Transmittal
NV5 will maintain accurate and comprehensive records related to all plans, calculations and documents
received. Our team is experienced in providing digital plan review and will accept, review and return plans
electronically if the City desires.
We will screen and log every application to assure they are routed to all plan checkers in a timely manner.

tracking device to assure turnarounds and completeness of review.

INTRODUCTION TO SA ASSOCIATES

SA Associates was established in May, 1989 as a principal-owned engineering firm with offices
in Los Angeles and Orange Counties. SA Associates is a California Corporation and “SA
Associates” is our full legal name. SA Associates services cover a broad spectrum of engineering
from investigation and feasibility reports to design, construction administration, and construction
observation. The firm provides complete civil engineering services for municipalities, public and
private water agencies, sanitary districts, and flood control districts. We are incorporated in the
State of California. We are committed to engineering excellence and principal involvement. SA
Associates currently has 22 employees. We are in stable financial condition.

QUALITY ASSURANCE/QUALITY CONTROL PROGRAM

It is the goal of SA Associates to present clients with a superior product and responsive service.
We are aware we can only continue to grow and remain a viable influence in the consulting
engineering profession if we produce an excellent product. That is why we have established
“excellence in engineering” as our credo. A sound company policy that emphasizes technical
strength, professional conduct, efficiency and communication is applied to each project in order
to achieve excellence. This policy is the basis of our Quality Assurance / Quality Control (QA/QC)
program.

To ensure quality, conformity, and enhanced client satisfaction, a uniform review and checking
procedure for all project documents is adopted and effectively applied through the QA/QC plan.
All project deliverables undergo two reviews to maintain high quality. The first review is
conducted by the QA/QC Manager to provide initial technical input, direction, and evaluation of
alternatives. The second review is a detailed, coordinated review by the QA/QC Manager with
selected lead personnel reflecting comments from the first review. This procedure ensures all
work is reviewed and checked prior to each submittal to the client. Each member of our team
makes it his/her responsibility to perform the services per the QA/QC program, and to ensure
that what is stated in writing or shown on drawings is correct, cost effective, and in conformance
with SA Associates’ standards.

PROJECT UNDERSTANDING
The city of South Gate is seeking qualified professional engineering firms to provide services on
an as needed basis covering the following areas including but not limited to: engineering and
architectural design, construction management, inspection, geotechnical, project management,
staff augmentation, surveying, special funding administration (intergovernmental agencies),
grant writing, plan review, right-of-way acquisition (with legal descriptions and appraisals),
assessment district engineering, estimating, arborist services, preparation of grant and federal
funding reimbursement requests, traffic and transportation engineering. The City plans to award
at least three (3) contracts for these requested services.
PROPOSED APPROACH AND WORK PLAN
Our approach to your projects is based on four principles that are essential for the success of
your project. These principles are:
1.  Providing the most qualified project manager and project team
2.  Ongoing communications with City Staff
3.  Direct principal involvement
4.  We are committed to providing you with a quality project and service.

We will implement and adhere to these principles continuously throughout the project.
Key Project issues that may be anticipated during design and construction
•  Utility Verification & Protection (Including Potholing As Necessary)
  Based on our experience with several recent projects on both the design and construction
  management side, we have the experience to ensure that utilities are located properly and
  protected during construction while minimizing risk of change orders to the City. To reduce
  costs associated with the protection of utilities and change orders during construction, the
  design will consider not only utility information provided from the City and underground utility
  companies, but also thorough field investigation and a strategic potholing plan (if authorized
  by the City). It will also be advantageous to provide for utility protection in the Bid Items
  descriptions in the measurement and payment section to emphasize utility protection and to
  avoid the risk of change orders. We have added a Geotechnical subconsultant firm on our
  team to cover any needed potholing.
•  Safety of Public
  It is of importance to maintain pedestrian and vehicular safety. It will also be important to
  provide proper barriers to keep public out of the work areas. This can be covered in part on
  the plans, under the General Notes and in the specifications. It will also be advantageous to
  provide for public safety in Bid Items descriptions in the Measurement and Payment section
  of the specifications to emphasize public safety and avoid the risk of change orders.

deteriorated  pull  boxes  and pedestrian  push  buttons,  intercepting  signal  service  and lighting
conduits  from  existing  traffic  signal  cabinets  and  isolating  the  interconnect  conduits.  This
additional  work  is included  for payment  under  proposed  Change  Order  Nos.  4 and 5, for a total
of $132,431.  Also  included  is $20,000 in liquidated  damages credited against the Contractor,
$38,828  for payment  of additional  unit quantities  of work,  and a $14,078 cost reduction for work
not performed.

The Council  is requested  to authorize  the City  Manager  to approve  the change  orders,  which  are
reasonable  as compared  to stipulated  construction  contract  costs.

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is in the FY 2022/23  Capital  Improvement  Program  ("CIP").  It
was implemented  to improve  pedestrian  and vehicular  safety  and relieve  traffic  congestion  on
Tweedy  Boulevard.  The  proposed  improvements  included  synchronizing  13 signalized  traffic
signals  on Tweedy  Boulevard,  between  Victoria  Avenue  and Atlantic  Avenue,  by physically
connecting  them  with  conduit  and fiber  optic  cabling;  upgrade  traffic  cabinets  and controllers;
re-wiring  traffic  signal  systems  at intersections;  installing  video  detection  systems;  and installing
artwork  on all new signal  cabinets.

On January  10, 2023,  the City  Council  approved  Contract  No. 2023-01-CC  with  the Contractor
for the construction  of the Project  in the amount  of $1,833,198.  Construction  began  on June 5,
2023,  and was completed  effective  May  31, 2024.  Work  was performed  in accordance  with  the
approved  specifications  with  acceptable  quality  and workmanship  within  budget  and time.  The
contractor  has met all of the contract  obligations.  The City  Council  may now  accept  the Project
as complete.  The Notice  of Completion  can now be filed  with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar
Recorder's  Office.

The final  construction  contract  amount  is $1,998,535.  This includes  the original  contract  amount
and the additional  quantities  constructed  of $1,872,026,  five  change  orders  with  a total 146,509,
and liquidated  damages  in the amount  of $20,0000.  This  change  order  also includes  additional
49 working  days.

  SUBJECT:  PURCHASE  ORDER  FOR  RENEWAL  OF SOFTWARE  MAINTENANCE
  AND  SUPPORT  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  WITH  HITECH  SYSTEMS,  INC.  DBA
  PULSIAM  FOR  THE  POLICE  DEPARTMENT

  PURPOSE:  To renew  the existing  contract  with  Hitech  Systems,  Inc. dba Pulsiam  ("Pulsiam")
  for  maintenance  and  support  services  agreement  which  includes  Computer  Aided  Dispatch
  ("CAD")  and Records  Management  Systems  ("RMS")  for the Police  Department.  South  Gate
  Municipal  Code requires  that all agreements  more than $50,000  be approved  by the City  Council.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  City  Council  will  consider  authorizing  the issuance  of a
  Purchase  Order  with  Pulsiam  to renew  the Software  Maintenance  and Support  Services  for Fiscal
  Year 2024/2025  for the Police  Department  in the amount  of $125,525.02.

  FISCALIMPACT:  Funds  for  these  services  were  included  in  the  Fiscal  Year  2024/25
  Municipal  Budget.

  ANALYSIS:  This  Purchase  Order  is for  the renewal  of  an existing  sole  source  proprietary
  software  agreement  that does not require  bidding  and complies  with  City  purchasing  guidelines.

  BACKGROUND:  For the past 30 years,  the Police  Department  has contracted  with  Pulsiam  to
  provide  24-hour  support  for its CAD  and RMS  systems.  The  CAD  and RMS  systems  are the
  foundation  of information  technology  that enables  the Police  Department  to receive  9-1-1  calls in
  the dispatch  center  and generate  calls for service  that are sent electronically  to police  officers  in

regular  business  meeting.  Amendments  should  be provided  to the City  Clerk's  Office  within  24

hours  of a City  Council  Meeting  so that  verification  of the record  and corrections  are made

accordingly.  A revised  document  will  be provided  to the City  Council  prior  to the Meeting.

BACKGROUND:  The minutes  typically  describe  the events  of the meeting  and may  include  a

list of attendees,  a statement  of the issues considered  by the participants,  and related  responses  or

decisions  for the issues.

SUBJECT:  UPDATE  OF CITY  COUNCIL  STRATEGIC  PRIORITY  PROJECTS  LIST

PURPOSE:  To present  an update  of the City  Council  Strategic  Priority  Projects.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider  receiving  and filing  an update  of
the Council  Strategic  Priority  Projects.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  The cost of any work  associated  with  the outlined  work  plan for the Council
Strategic  priority  projects  are already  contained  within  the 2024-25  Budget.

ANALYSIS:  The  City  Council  directed  the City  Manager  to organize  a Strategic  Planning
Workshop  to develop  a Strategic  Plan. The purpose  of this effort  is to provide  a focus on the most
important  goals that the City  Council  has for the community  to guide City  staff in what they should
focus on. The Priority  Project  list that was created  is now the focus of staff efforts  to complete.

BACKGROUND:  The City  Council,  City  Manager,  City  Attorney,  and Department  Heads  met
on March  28, 2024,  at the Azalea  room  to hold  a Strategic  Planning  session.  This  meeting  was
facilitated  by consultant  Jacob  Green.  Jacob  Green  conducted  one-on-one  interviews  with  City
Council  Members  and the City  Manager  prior  to the workshop  to help shape the agenda of the day.
The workshop  included  a discussion  on the origins  of the City  Council  - City  Manager  form  of
governrnent,  best practices  in City governance,  and the importance  of setting  priority  goals to focus
organizational  effort.  A list of priority  projects  was created  and a regular  update  on progress  is to
be presented  to the City  Council.

Priority  Goals  - By the conclusion  of the workshop,  the Council  had developed  a priority  goal list
that contained  six core goals,  each with  several  sub points  to describe  the specifics  of the goal.
This list is attached  and contains  the following  top six goal areas:

  *  Public  Safety
  *  Fiscal  Sustainability
  *  Infirastruchire
  *  Cornrnunity  Outreach  and Engagement

   *  Community/Economic  Development  and Housing
  *  Organizational  Excellence

Over  the course  of the coming  year,  the City  will  be ensuring  these goals  are top of mind  and
prioritized  when  determining  how  to allocate  staffing  resources.  The  first  update  on project
progress  is contained  in the attached  project  spreadsheet.

Priority  Projects  - The City  Manager  and Department  Heads reviewed  the Council  priority  goal
list, and after discussion,  created  a priority  project  list that creates specific  projects  with  assigned
staff  and milestone  deliverable  dates  to focus  efforts  and provide  results.  These  projects  are
focused  on furthering  the goals  set by the City  Council.  With  limited  staffing  resources,  the list
provides  a realistic  assignment  of staffing  resources  with  proposed  timelines  for deliverables  that
staff feel are achievable.
